steps.line: E·r is the same on every shell
steps.because: and the same numbers read as an energy rather than as a balance: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so E·r is the coupling again up to a factor that is the same on every shell. Measured, it moves by 0.00 per cent across n = 1 to 4. It is NOT a second measurement - it is the first one read the other way, and saying so is the difference between two premises and one premise counted twice

measured.name: E·r
measured.note: E·r at n = 1, and across n = 1 to 4 it is -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2 - a spread of 0.00 per cent. IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON WHICH SHELL, which is the whole of what makes this one atom rather than a different force at every radius: the coupling is a property of the two bodies' biases and of nothing else

steps.because: and the same coupling read as an energy: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so an energy times a radius is that coupling again up to a factor which is also the same on every shell. This is not a second premise - it is the first one written the other way, which is why the run reports one measurement behind both
E·r cannot change, and written out it is E_{n}·r_{n}. E_{n} carries the exponent 1 there, so holding the product fixed pins E_{n} to the rest raised to -1

steps.line: p^{2}r is the same on every shell
steps.because: what holds a thing in a circle is its momentum against the pull, and the pull here is the sign law's coupling over r^{2} - so p^{2}/r = g_q/r^{2} and p^{2}r is the coupling itself. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES AND OF NOTHING ELSE, so it cannot depend on which shell is being asked about - measured across the four lowest, it moves by 0.00 per cent

measured.name: p^{2}r
measured.note: p^{2}r at n = 1, taken as 2·(-E)·r since what is not potential is kinetic - across n = 1 to 4 it is 6.250e-2, 6.250e-2, 6.250e-2, 6.250e-2, a spread of 0.00 per cent. The same numbers as E·r read as the force balance rather than as the energy, and constant for the same reason

measured.name: E·r
measured.note: E·r at n = 1, and across n = 1 to 4 it is -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2 - a spread of 0.00 per cent. IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON WHICH SHELL, which is the whole of what makes this one atom rather than a different force at every radius: the coupling is a property of the two bodies' biases and of nothing else

steps.because: and what the balance holds fixed is momentum twice and radius once. What keeps a thing on a curve goes as p^{2}/r and what pulls it goes as g_q/r^{2} - charge.attraction's coupling over charge.falloff's room - so setting the two equal leaves p^{2}r = g_q, with the inverse square already divided out. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES, so it is the same on every shell, and the run measured that rather than assuming it

matter.debroglie established that a region holds a whole number of nodes and that this comes to p·r = n·pi·hbar. Neither pi nor hbar has anything to do with which shell is being asked about, so as a statement about how the momentum moves when the shell does, it is p ∝ n/r. The constants are not lost - they are in the line that is cited, and they set the SIZE of the atom rather than the shape of the ladder

p^{2}r cannot change, and written out it is \frac{nodes^{2}}{r_{n}}. r_{n} carries the exponent -1 there - it appears more than once, because the factors are not all independent of it, so holding the product fixed pins r_{n} to the rest raised to 1
r_{n} is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

steps.because: and the same numbers read as an energy rather than as a balance: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so E·r is the coupling again up to a factor that is the same on every shell. steps.because: what holds a thing in a circle is its momentum against the pull, and the pull here is the sign law's coupling over r^{2} - so p^{2}/r = g_q/r^{2} and p^{2}r is the coupling itself. steps.because: and what the balance holds fixed is momentum twice and radius once. What keeps a thing on a curve goes as p^{2}/r and what pulls it goes as g_q/r^{2} - charge.attraction's coupling over charge.falloff's room - so setting the two equal leaves p^{2}r = g_q, with the inverse square already divided out. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES, so it is the same on every shell, and the run measured that rather than assuming it

matter.debroglie established that a region holds a whole number of nodes and that this comes to p·r = n·pi·hbar. Neither pi nor hbar has anything to do with which shell is being asked about, so as a statement about how the momentum moves when the shell does, it is p ∝ n/r. The constants are not lost - they are in the line that is cited, and they set the SIZE of the atom rather than the shape of the ladder

p^{2}r cannot change, and written out it is \frac{nodes^{2}}{r_{n}}. r_{n} carries the exponent -1 there - it appears more than once, because the factors are not all independent of it, so holding the product fixed pins r_{n} to the rest raised to 1
r_{n} is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

steps.line: E·r is the same on every shell
steps.because: and the same numbers read as an energy rather than as a balance: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so E·r is the coupling again up to a factor that is the same on every shell. Measured, it moves by 0.00 per cent across n = 1 to 4. It is NOT a second measurement - it is the first one read the other way, and saying so is the difference between two premises and one premise counted twice

measured.name: E·r
measured.note: E·r at n = 1, and across n = 1 to 4 it is -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2 - a spread of 0.00 per cent. IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON WHICH SHELL, which is the whole of what makes this one atom rather than a different force at every radius: the coupling is a property of the two bodies' biases and of nothing else

steps.because: and the same coupling read as an energy: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so an energy times a radius is that coupling again up to a factor which is also the same on every shell. This is not a second premise - it is the first one written the other way, which is why the run reports one measurement behind both
E·r cannot change, and written out it is E_{n}·r_{n}. E_{n} carries the exponent 1 there, so holding the product fixed pins E_{n} to the rest raised to -1

steps.line: p^{2}r is the same on every shell
steps.because: what holds a thing in a circle is its momentum against the pull, and the pull here is the sign law's coupling over r^{2} - so p^{2}/r = g_q/r^{2} and p^{2}r is the coupling itself. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES AND OF NOTHING ELSE, so it cannot depend on which shell is being asked about - measured across the four lowest, it moves by 0.00 per cent

measured.name: p^{2}r
measured.note: p^{2}r at n = 1, taken as 2·(-E)·r since what is not potential is kinetic - across n = 1 to 4 it is 6.250e-2, 6.250e-2, 6.250e-2, 6.250e-2, a spread of 0.00 per cent. The same numbers as E·r read as the force balance rather than as the energy, and constant for the same reason

measured.name: E·r
measured.note: E·r at n = 1, and across n = 1 to 4 it is -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2 - a spread of 0.00 per cent. IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON WHICH SHELL, which is the whole of what makes this one atom rather than a different force at every radius: the coupling is a property of the two bodies' biases and of nothing else

steps.because: and what the balance holds fixed is momentum twice and radius once. What keeps a thing on a curve goes as p^{2}/r and what pulls it goes as g_q/r^{2} - charge.attraction's coupling over charge.falloff's room - so setting the two equal leaves p^{2}r = g_q, with the inverse square already divided out. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES, so it is the same on every shell, and the run measured that rather than assuming it

matter.debroglie established that a region holds a whole number of nodes and that this comes to p·r = n·pi·hbar. Neither pi nor hbar has anything to do with which shell is being asked about, so as a statement about how the momentum moves when the shell does, it is p ∝ n/r. The constants are not lost - they are in the line that is cited, and they set the SIZE of the atom rather than the shape of the ladder

p^{2}r cannot change, and written out it is \frac{nodes^{2}}{r_{n}}. r_{n} carries the exponent -1 there - it appears more than once, because the factors are not all independent of it, so holding the product fixed pins r_{n} to the rest raised to 1
r_{n} is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

E_{n}.says: what it would take to get the thing off the n-th shell

r_{n}.says: how far out that shell stands

nodes.says: how many nodes fit - counted off the solution, not imposed

p.says: the momentum of what is standing there

p^{2}r.says: what the balance holds fixed - the momentum against the pull, which comes to the coupling itself

E·r.says: the same statement read as an energy rather than as a balance

g_{q}.says: how much of the unbiased pull this pair gets - charge.attraction's (1 - P_a·P_b), which is 2 for an atom and 0 for two alike

\\pi.says: the boundary factor matter.debroglie carries and does not absorb

variants.asks: one body biased one way, one the other. The sign law says what they pull with and the counting condition says what can stand in it - so how far out are the shells, and what does it take to get off one?

probes.asks: the sign law says what a biased pair pulls with and the counting condition says what can stand in it. Put both on the lattice at once: what is bound, how far out, and where is it actually found?
probes.found: the two laws together bind: 10 states stand in the well, each with n - l - 1 nodes in its radius - counted off its own solution, and whole in every one of them. The coupling comes out the same on every shell to 0.00 per cent, the mean radius goes as n^{2.001} and the energy as n^{-2.001}. At ALIKE biases the coupling is nought, there is no well, and nothing is bound - which is the sign law's own prediction and the control this rests on

measured.name: g_{q}
measured.note: 1 - P_a·P_b at P_a = +1 against P_b = -1, which is what an atom is: one body biased one way and one the other. Twice what unbiased matter of the same masses would feel, and it is charge.attraction's number rather than this probe's

measured.name: bound states at alike bias
measured.note: the control, and it is the sign law with its teeth in: two bodies biased the SAME way have 1 - P_a·P_b = 0, so there is no well at all and nothing can stand in it. Nought here is the prediction; anything else would refute charge.attraction

steps.because: and what the balance holds fixed is momentum twice and radius once. steps.because: and the same numbers read as an energy rather than as a balance: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so E·r is the coupling again up to a factor that is the same on every shell. steps.line: p^{2}r is the same on every shell
steps.because: what holds a thing in a circle is its momentum against the pull, and the pull here is the sign law's coupling over r^{2} - so p^{2}/r = g_q/r^{2} and p^{2}r is the coupling itself. steps.because: and what the balance holds fixed is momentum twice and radius once. What keeps a thing on a curve goes as p^{2}/r and what pulls it goes as g_q/r^{2} - charge.attraction's coupling over charge.falloff's room - so setting the two equal leaves p^{2}r = g_q, with the inverse square already divided out. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES, so it is the same on every shell, and the run measured that rather than assuming it

matter.debroglie established that a region holds a whole number of nodes and that this comes to p·r = n·pi·hbar. Neither pi nor hbar has anything to do with which shell is being asked about, so as a statement about how the momentum moves when the shell does, it is p ∝ n/r. The constants are not lost - they are in the line that is cited, and they set the SIZE of the atom rather than the shape of the ladder

p^{2}r cannot change, and written out it is \frac{nodes^{2}}{r_{n}}. r_{n} carries the exponent -1 there - it appears more than once, because the factors are not all independent of it, so holding the product fixed pins r_{n} to the rest raised to 1
r_{n} is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

steps.line: E·r is the same on every shell
steps.because: and the same numbers read as an energy rather than as a balance: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so E·r is the coupling again up to a factor that is the same on every shell. Measured, it moves by 0.00 per cent across n = 1 to 4. It is NOT a second measurement - it is the first one read the other way, and saying so is the difference between two premises and one premise counted twice

measured.name: E·r
measured.note: E·r at n = 1, and across n = 1 to 4 it is -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2 - a spread of 0.00 per cent. IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON WHICH SHELL, which is the whole of what makes this one atom rather than a different force at every radius: the coupling is a property of the two bodies' biases and of nothing else

steps.because: and the same coupling read as an energy: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so an energy times a radius is that coupling again up to a factor which is also the same on every shell. This is not a second premise - it is the first one written the other way, which is why the run reports one measurement behind both
E·r cannot change, and written out it is E_{n}·r_{n}. E_{n} carries the exponent 1 there, so holding the product fixed pins E_{n} to the rest raised to -1

steps.line: p^{2}r is the same on every shell
steps.because: what holds a thing in a circle is its momentum against the pull, and the pull here is the sign law's coupling over r^{2} - so p^{2}/r = g_q/r^{2} and p^{2}r is the coupling itself. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES AND OF NOTHING ELSE, so it cannot depend on which shell is being asked about - measured across the four lowest, it moves by 0.00 per cent

measured.name: p^{2}r
measured.note: p^{2}r at n = 1, taken as 2·(-E)·r since what is not potential is kinetic - across n = 1 to 4 it is 6.250e-2, 6.250e-2, 6.250e-2, 6.250e-2, a spread of 0.00 per cent. The same numbers as E·r read as the force balance rather than as the energy, and constant for the same reason

measured.name: E·r
measured.note: E·r at n = 1, and across n = 1 to 4 it is -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2, -3.125e-2 - a spread of 0.00 per cent. IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON WHICH SHELL, which is the whole of what makes this one atom rather than a different force at every radius: the coupling is a property of the two bodies' biases and of nothing else

steps.because: and what the balance holds fixed is momentum twice and radius once. What keeps a thing on a curve goes as p^{2}/r and what pulls it goes as g_q/r^{2} - charge.attraction's coupling over charge.falloff's room - so setting the two equal leaves p^{2}r = g_q, with the inverse square already divided out. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES, so it is the same on every shell, and the run measured that rather than assuming it

matter.debroglie established that a region holds a whole number of nodes and that this comes to p·r = n·pi·hbar. Neither pi nor hbar has anything to do with which shell is being asked about, so as a statement about how the momentum moves when the shell does, it is p ∝ n/r. The constants are not lost - they are in the line that is cited, and they set the SIZE of the atom rather than the shape of the ladder

p^{2}r cannot change, and written out it is \frac{nodes^{2}}{r_{n}}. r_{n} carries the exponent -1 there - it appears more than once, because the factors are not all independent of it, so holding the product fixed pins r_{n} to the rest raised to 1
r_{n} is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

E_{n}.says: what it would take to get the thing off the n-th shell

r_{n}.says: how far out that shell stands

nodes.says: how many nodes fit - counted off the solution, not imposed

p.says: the momentum of what is standing there

p^{2}r.says: what the balance holds fixed - the momentum against the pull, which comes to the coupling itself

E·r.says: the same statement read as an energy rather than as a balance

g_{q}.says: how much of the unbiased pull this pair gets - charge.attraction's (1 - P_a·P_b), which is 2 for an atom and 0 for two alike

\\pi.says: the boundary factor matter.debroglie carries and does not absorb

variants.asks: one body biased one way, one the other. The sign law says what they pull with and the counting condition says what can stand in it - so how far out are the shells, and what does it take to get off one?

probes.asks: the sign law says what a biased pair pulls with and the counting condition says what can stand in it. Put both on the lattice at once: what is bound, how far out, and where is it actually found?
probes.found: the two laws together bind: 10 states stand in the well, each with n - l - 1 nodes in its radius - counted off its own solution, and whole in every one of them. The coupling comes out the same on every shell to 0.00 per cent, the mean radius goes as n^{2.001} and the energy as n^{-2.001}. At ALIKE biases the coupling is nought, there is no well, and nothing is bound - which is the sign law's own prediction and the control this rests on

measured.name: g_{q}
measured.note: 1 - P_a·P_b at P_a = +1 against P_b = -1, which is what an atom is: one body biased one way and one the other. Twice what unbiased matter of the same masses would feel, and it is charge.attraction's number rather than this probe's

measured.name: bound states at alike bias
measured.note: the control, and it is the sign law with its teeth in: two bodies biased the SAME way have 1 - P_a·P_b = 0, so there is no well at all and nothing can stand in it. Nought here is the prediction; anything else would refute charge.attraction
